title: The Solid Made of Air
hook: A piece of frozen smoke can stop a blowtorch flame from burning your hand.
script: A piece of frozen smoke can stop a blowtorch flame from burning your hand. How can a solid that is 99.8 percent air block thousands of degrees? Chemist Samuel Kistler created aerogel in 1931 after a bet over drying fruit jelly. Though it looks like trapped cloud, aerogel tinkles like hard candy when dropped on glass. Heat fails to cross because microscopic pores stop air molecules from touching each other. Inside, one gram contains enough folded surface to stretch across three full tennis courts. NASA used it to trap hypersonic comet dust without melting the tiny particles. Holding over a dozen world records, it scatters light just like Earth's atmosphere does.
